response.text: {"question":"What is the dynamical role of tumour-evoked regulatory B cells in breast cancer immune response and how do they influence tumour growth and metastasis?","mechanism":"Breast cancer cells grow logistically and are killed by NK cells; Tregs suppress NK cells; tBregs are activated by tumour cells and increase Tregs; Tregs in turn suppress NK cells, reducing tumour killing.","modelEquations":["eq2","eq3"],"result":{"text":"The model shows tumour-evoked regulatory B cells promote breast cancer growth by suppressing NK cells via Tregs, allowing the tumour to reach carrying capacity and increasing metastatic potential.","quote":"It serves for a compact study of the dynamical role in cancer promotion of a relatively recently described subgroup of regulatory B cells, which are evoked by the tumour."},"findings":[{"kind":"threshold","text":"Admissible equilibrium E2 exists only when the NK-induced tumour death rate is below a threshold.","quote":"Admissible equilibrium point $E_2$ exists when $c\\leq c_1$."},{"kind":"threshold","text":"Admissible equilibrium E3 requires c >= c2 and theta_B/m_T < 1/b.","quote":"Admissible equilibrium point $E_3$ exists when $c\\geq c_2$ and $\\frac{\\theta_B}{m_T} < \\frac{1}{b}$."},{"kind":"result","text":"E1 is locally asymptotically stable for c >= c1 and unstable for c < c1.","quote":"E_1 always exists, and is locally stable when $c \\ge c_1$, and unstable when $c < c_1$."},{"kind":"result","text":"No closed orbits and hence no Hopf bifurcation occur when theta_B/m_T > 1/b.","quote":"If $0\\leq T_0\\leq \\frac{1}{b}\\text{ and }\\frac{\\theta_B}{m_T} > \\frac{1}{b}$, then IVP has no closed orbits and therefore a Hopf bifurcation can not occur."},{"kind":"conclusion","text":"With tBregs present and tumour carrying capacity bounded from above, the tumour initially reaches carrying capacity due to tBregs.","quote":"Conclusion 2: In the presence of tBregs, if tumour carrying capacity is bounded from above, then the breast tumour will initially reach its carrying capacity due to the effect of tBregs, i.e. initially $T \\nearrow \\frac{1}{b}$ when $B_0 \\nearrow $."}]}
